title: Preemptive Detection of Fake Accounts on Social Networks via Multi-Class Preferential Attachment Classifiers

problem.claim: Detect fake accounts in a social network.

gap.claim: Existing high-accuracy algorithms rely on fake-account friendship or shared-content information that detection aims to prevent.

contributions.claim: Preferential Attachment k-class Classifier (PreAttacK), an algorithm for detecting fake accounts in a social network.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe PreAttacK as a new algorithm.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper addresses fake-account detection in social networks.
Several existing algorithms reportedly achieve high accuracy.
Those algorithms rely on friendship or shared-content information associated with fake accounts.
The paper introduces PreAttacK for fake-account detection.

source_observation.claim: High-accuracy detection methods may rely on information that the detection system seeks to prevent or avoid using.

interpretation.claim: Detection quality should be considered alongside whether the required signals are available before or independent of the target behavior.

application.claim: When designing preemptive detection systems, evaluate whether features are available without relying on the prohibited or unavailable information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when such information is unavailable, prohibited, or harmful in a specific deployment.

unknowns: No detection results or quantitative performance are reported.
No dataset, experimental setup, baseline comparison, or evaluation protocol is supplied.
The abstract does not specify the features, classifier formulation, or meaning of k-class.
No evidence is supplied about preemptive detection performance or deployment conditions.
